newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Telecom to take Clear to court.
newsitem.headline: Telecom to take Clear to court.

text.p: Telecommunications company Telecom New Zealand Ltd said on Thursday it planned to take rival Clear Communications to court, in order to get payment for what it alleged were unpaid bills.
Telecom said Clear already owed it over NZ$1 million.
It said the two firms signed a commercial agreement a year ago, where Telecom would supply Clear with services allowing Clear to interconnect its network with Telecom's.
Prices were agreed at the time and set for a five year term, Telecom said.

"Since then, we have been supplying the services. Clear initially paid for them at the agreed prices. Then, last August... Clear told us it did not like some of the prices in the agreement and wanted them changed," Telecom said.
It said that since February Clear had refused to pay what it initially agreed to pay.
Telecom said that as Clear was 50 percent owned by two of the world's largest telecommunications companies, British Telecom and MCI Communications Corp, it could afford to pay its bills.
The New Zealand family-owned Todd Corporation and state-owned Television New Zealand own the other half of Clear.
A spokeswoman for Clear told Reuters the company had only just heard of Telecom's announcement through the media and would be releasing a statement shortly.
